title: The revolt of 14 May restores the Democrats
summary: Armed civilians, naval units and part of the Lisbon garrison rose on 14 May 1915 against the government of General Pimenta de Castro, which had been appointed by President Manuel de Arriaga and had governed without parliament while readmitting monarchists to public life. Several days of fighting in the capital left hundreds dead and wounded before the government surrendered; Pimenta de Castro and Arriaga were removed and the Democratic Party returned to power. The revolt settled the immediate question in favour of the party, and settled nothing about the method: force had again decided a political dispute, and it did so again in 1917, 1919, 1921 and 1926. It is in the atlas as an early link in the chain of interventions that ends with the First Republic's fall.
